excerpts:
About us
We build Kaiten. Then we run on it.
Kaiten is the control plane for B2B SaaS: one model for what each customer bought, what they can use and what runs for them. We are four engineers, all co-founders, at Station F in Paris — and our own releases, hosted environments and Kaiten Cloud organizations live in our own Kaiten, so we meet its rough edges before you do.
Kaiten is built by four engineers — all co-founders — at Station F in Paris. Each of us had built the same thing before, by hand, in the SaaS companies we come from: the code that decides what a product does for each customer. Kaiten is that code, built once, as infrastructure.
How Kaiten started.
1. 01
We built it before
Each of us had built this second product by hand in the SaaS companies we come from: a licensing service here, a flag wrapper there, a spreadsheet of who runs which version.
2. 02
We looked for it elsewhere
Four engineers, all co-founders. We started Kaiten at Station F after years of building this kind of infrastructure together.
Alexandre Bergere Alexandre Bergere
Alexandre Bergere
Alexandre co-founded Kaiten to eradicate 'Spaghetti SaaS' and the practice of hardcoding pricing plans, building an open-source control plane that restores engineering freedom by decoupling business logic from the codebase.

citations.title: Kaiten | Why Kaiten — The Missing Layer Between Your Business ...
excerpts:
Argo CD, Flux or your CI keep deploying. Kaiten records which release runs where, and for whom.
*
A data warehouse
Your warehouse keeps the analysis. Kaiten emits a typed event for every change it records.
*
A general-purpose automation tool
Kaiten is for teams that already shipped something and now operate it across many customers, regions and pricing tiers. Below that threshold, you don’t need us. Above it, the glue code starts costing more than the product it connects.
* Best fit
B2B SaaS selling negotiated enterprise contracts
* Costs per token, per model or per call
* Pricing that moves with those costs
* Each customer’s AI consumption metered and capped — AI credits are an entitlement type today
* Per-model conversion rules — on the roadmap
* Strong fit
Regulated SaaS with dedicated deployments
* Customers in banking, defense or healthcare who require isolation
* Ground truth on which release runs for which customer
* An audit trail you can query instead of logs you grep
* Self-hosted on your own Kubernetes today — an air-gapped runtime is on the roadmap
* Emerging fit
Apps built by coding agents
* You only sell self-serve consumer subscriptions — your billing provider’s customer portal is enough on its own.
* You have one plan and one region — a config file will do.
  See what each team does in Kaiten

Three horizons, one question each.
